"Add the lightsaber duel mode to our game. (The one we discussed before, we already have a button for it in activities) All custom lightsabers have equal base stats so parts are purely cosmetic and free. The player grows stronger and levels up by winning more battles. Include stance selection and simple turn-based combat choices like attacking, heavy striking, blocking, or using force pushes. For the visuals, keep it simple with a basic side-view showing two characters with glowing colored blade lines swinging at each other. Also when entering the duel mode, let the player pick a lightsaber from their collection they have already made, so for minigame you should convert the 3d models to work in 2d, so you need to flatten them basically, because of the side view ehen battling

13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

## Objective
- Add a complete, playable lightsaber duel mode to the existing game, accessible through the existing Activities button.
- Let players choose a collected saber and stance, fight turn-based battles, and gain strength and levels through wins.

## Requirements
- Custom saber parts are free and cosmetic; all sabers have equal base stats.
- Include attack, heavy strike, block, and Force Push choices.
- Use a simple side-view with two characters and glowing blade lines; flatten/represent collected 3D sabers in 2D for the duel.
- Build and verify the feature without asking clarifying questions; note reasonable assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a local duel record key, `sabersmith.duel.v1`, for progress.
- Planned stances: Shii-Cho (balanced), Soresu (defensive), and Djem So (aggressive).
- Planned controls include action buttons and keyboard keys `1`–`4`.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` was edited to add a duel stylesheet reference, duel overlay/lobby/arena markup, and to update the existing Training Duel activity card.
- `duel.css` was created with styling for the duel interface.
- `game.js` was edited to wire the activity button to `openDuel()` and include duel overlay state in some existing overlay/keyboard checks.

### Active
- Duel gameplay JavaScript implementation was attempted in `game.js`, but the edit tool returned an error; verify whether any of that implementation landed. The duel markup currently depends on functions and state such as `openDuel`, `closeDuel`, and `duel`.
- Finish implementing the duel flow, including saber selection from the collection, flattened 2D preview, combat, victory progression, and persistence.
- Run the game and verify it works, including a screenshot check.

### Blocked
- The attempted large `game.js` insertion failed with a tool error, so the duel feature may currently be incomplete or broken.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `game.js`, `index.html`, and `duel.css` to establish exactly what edits landed.
2. Implement or repair the missing duel JavaScript and connect it to existing collection data and game lifecycle.
3. Run the game, test lobby selection and multiple combat outcomes, and check responsive rendering.
4. Report assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Duel activity card and overlay markup.
- `game.js`: Existing game logic and partial duel event wiring; main implementation remains to be verified.
- `duel.css`: New duel UI styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The assistant described a planned duel implementation, but the large `game.js` edit failed; do not assume the full implementation exists.

## Objective
- Add a complete, playable lightsaber duel mode accessible through **Activities → Training Duel**, with saber and stance selection, turn-based combat, and win-based progression.

- Custom saber parts are free and cosmetic; all sabers have equal base stats.

- Defeats grant no XP; strength progression comes from wins.
